name: 2D-Grid-Cursor
summary: In handheld AR, a translucent flat grid cursor is placed in the scene; vertical swipes move it in depth and horizontal swipes resize it, and tapping the grid cell over the target selects it.
howItWorks: Touching places the grid cursor at the touch point; swiping up or down pushes it deeper or pulls it closer, and left or right changes its size. Objects the grid passes through are shown in its cells and a tap on the right cell selects. On an iPhone 6 with 12 participants (targets 0.2–1 cm, 20–80% occluded), error rates were 0.25% for PR-Bubble-Cursor, 1.2% for PR-Cone-Casting, 2.7% for touch Go-Go, 4.4% for 2D-Grid-Cursor, 5% for Offset-Ray-Casting and 41% for touch raycasting; times were 0.44 s for raycasting, 0.68 s PR-Cone, 1.22 s Offset, 1.29 s PR-Bubble, 2.06 s Grid and 2.75 s Go-Go. PR-Bubble-Cursor was preferred.

relationships.note: Compared with a touch version of Go-Go where a swipe sets arm length.
